careers.subtitle: Join the team building the future of decentralised social media
careers.intro: We're looking for passionate individuals who want to be part of the next wave of social media — one that puts creators and communities first. All roles are fully remote with flexible hours.
careers.bdmAbout: As one of our Business Development Managers at DeHub, you will be part of the driving force behind our partnership strategy. Your mission is to identify, engage, and close deals with companies across both Web2 and Web3 — from gaming studios and content platforms to blockchain projects and DeFi protocols. This is an OTE (On-Target Earnings) commission-based position: the harder you hustle, the more you earn. The role is simple, bring on companies, projects, communities or any large profile accounts on to DeHub, and get paid.
careers.bdmResp1: Identify and secure strategic partnerships with Web2 and Web3 companies that align with DeHub's mission
careers.bdmResp2: Build and manage a pipeline of prospective partners, sponsors, and integration opportunities
careers.bdmResp3: Represent DeHub at industry events, conferences, and virtual summits
careers.bdmResp4: Negotiate partnership terms, revenue-sharing models, and co-marketing agreements
careers.bdmResp5: Collaborate with the product and marketing teams to develop joint campaigns and integrations
careers.bdmReq1: Proven experience in business development, partnerships, or sales within tech, gaming, or Web3
careers.bdmReq2: Strong existing network in the crypto/Web3 or creator economy space is a huge plus
careers.bdmReq3: Excellent communication and negotiation skills — you can close deals and build lasting relationships
careers.bdmReq4: Self-motivated and comfortable working autonomously in a remote-first environment
careers.bdmReq5: Genuine interest in decentralised social media, NFTs, or blockchain technology
careers.bdmComp: This role offers a negotiable base salary plus an uncapped OTE commission structure tied directly to the partnerships you bring in. Top performers have unlimited earning potential.
careers.ambassadorAbout: As a DeHub Brand Ambassador you are the face and voice of the platform in your community. Your job is to spread the word about DeHub across every channel you touch — social media, IRL meetups, gaming events, university campuses, and beyond. This is a paid monthly salary role, not commission-based; you'll earn a consistent income while growing alongside the platform.

proof.title: Where these numbers come from
proof.subtitle: Measured by Cloudflare, not by this page
proof.query: The exact query behind the chart
proof.edge: Every request to dehub.io passes through Cloudflare before it reaches our servers. These counts are Cloudflare’s own aggregation of that traffic — the same figures our dashboard shows. They are not collected by a script in your browser, so nothing on this page can inflate them, and blocking trackers does not change them.
proof.live: The page reads them live. Loading /stats calls our endpoint, which queries Cloudflare’s Analytics API at that moment and caches the answer for 60 seconds.
proof.limits: What this shows, and what it does not: you can see that the figures come from Cloudflare’s aggregation rather than from our application code, and that the query published here is the one that runs. It is not trustless — we hold the API token, and Cloudflare offers no public read of a zone’s analytics. Anyone with their own Cloudflare zone can run the identical query against it and confirm the shape.

definitions.title: What the numbers mean
definitions.visitors: — unique IP addresses Cloudflare saw that day. Close to people, but not identical: an office on one connection counts once, and a phone moving between wifi and mobile data counts twice.
definitions.pageViews: — requests Cloudflare classifies as page loads, rather than images, scripts or API calls.
definitions.bots: — these are raw edge counts, so crawlers, uptime monitors and scripted clients are in them. You can see them yourself in the browser breakdown above, where entries like “Curl” and “Unknown” are automated traffic rather than people. Filtering bots out needs a paid Cloudflare tier we do not run, and quietly subtracting an estimate would make the numbers less checkable, not more.
definitions.total: — page views and requests add up across the range. Visitor counts deliberately are not summed into a headline "total visitors", because someone here on Monday and Tuesday would be counted twice.
definitions.peak: — the highest unique count in any single bucket of the range, for the same reason: it is a figure Cloudflare actually measures, rather than one built by adding counts that overlap.
definitions.resolution: — that is Cloudflare’s limit on this plan, not a choice: it refuses any hourly query wider than three days. The 24-hour and 3-day views are hourly; 7 days and longer are daily, and there is no way to draw an hourly all-time chart.
definitions.breakdown: — these follow the range you pick, but only back {{max}} days, which is as far as the per-day breakdown is kept. On longer ranges the chart covers more time than the country list does.
definitions.start: — "all time" means every day Cloudflare still retains, which today is {{days}} days starting {{date}}, the day dehub.io moved onto Cloudflare. There is no earlier edge data to show, and older days drop off as Cloudflare ages them out.

depin.heroCaption: DeHub keeps the origin copy. Community nodes add resilient replicas and local delivery capacity.
depin.earlyAccessBody: A lightweight, browser-based node is live below. A heavier, always-on desktop node is a stated future direction, not available yet. Participation never guarantees a reward.
depin.runFromTabTitle: Run a node from this tab.
depin.runFromTabBody: No install, no download. Sign in, opt in, and your open browser tab starts holding a second copy of a few DeHub media objects.
depin.signInBlurb: Sign in to turn this browser tab into a lightweight backup node.
depin.optInBlurb: This tier runs entirely in your browser using local storage (OPFS). It contributes only while this tab stays open — closing it stops your node, and reopening it starts a new one. There is no install and nothing runs in the background.
depin.unsupportedBlurb: Browser storage nodes need Origin Private File System support, which this browser does not offer (this is common on Safari). Try a recent Chrome, Edge or Firefox instead.
depin.rejectedBlurb: The network refused this node's session, which usually means it expired while the page was open. Sign in again and opt in — nothing was lost.
depin.threeJobsBody: Operators choose their storage, bandwidth and compute limits. DeHub schedules only the work their machine can safely handle.
depin.transcodeImageAlt: A home creator workstation contributing spare GPU compute
depin.transcodeBody: Eligible machines turn uploaded video into adaptive renditions. Every output is checked before it can be served.
depin.hostBody: Nodes keep encrypted or content-addressed segments in a capped local cache. DeHub origin storage remains the source of truth.
depin.deliverBody: Nearby peers share video segments while the normal delivery path stays ready as an automatic fallback.
depin.nodesLeaveTitle: A network that expects nodes to leave.
depin.nodesLeaveBody: No community machine holds the only copy. Health checks, replicas and origin fallback keep playback available.
depin.originBody: Permanent source copy and fallback delivery
depin.availableReplicasBody: Serve verified segments close to demand
depin.offlineNodeBody: Removed from routing until it reconnects
depin.viewerBody: Uses a peer when available, origin when needed
depin.privacyBody: Protected media stays encrypted on community hardware. Playback keys are issued separately to authorised viewers.
depin.protectedContentBody: Subscriber, private and pay-per-view segments can be stored as ciphertext. Node operators do not receive entitlement keys simply because they host data.
depin.publicContentBody: Encryption prevents casual inspection of cached files, but public media remains watchable through the public DeHub player. We will not claim otherwise.
depin.operatorControlsBody: Operators choose disk limits, bandwidth limits, working hours and eligible public content categories. Removal notices trigger cache purges.
depin.verifiedWorkTitle: Useful work is verified. Rewards stay variable.
depin.verifiedWorkBody: Contribution is measured through signed receipts, health checks and output validation. Storage alone does not create a reward.
depin.deliveryReceiptsBody: Verified bytes served to real playback sessions.
depin.availabilityBody: Successful retrieval checks and reliable service when assigned.
depin.validOutputBody: Transcodes must pass technical and sampled quality checks.
depin.revenuePoolBody: If activated, a reward budget would be set from platform revenue after the epoch closes.
depin.noFixedRate: There is no fixed rate, minimum return, APY or forward estimate. Contribution records are accounting inputs only, not a promise of payment. Any future DHB settlement would occur on Base and remain subject to eligibility, network rules and applicable law.
depin.runningCosts: Running a node uses electricity, internet data and hardware life. Operators may receive nothing, and their costs may exceed any reward.
depin.safestWorkloadTitle: Built from the safest workload outward.
depin.safestWorkloadBody: DePin supplements DeHub's existing delivery path first. More demanding workloads follow only after verification is proven.
depin.deliveryBody: Peer-assisted live and video delivery with automatic fallback.
depin.adaptiveVideoBody: Multiple renditions for reliable playback across connection speeds.
depin.desktopNodesBody: Capped storage, bandwidth controls and verified availability.
depin.baseSettlementBody: Revenue-funded claims only after operational and legal review.
depin.faqOfflineQ: What happens when a hosting node goes offline?
depin.faqOfflineA: The coordinator removes it from active routing. Another replica serves the segment, or playback falls back to DeHub origin storage while replacement copies are scheduled.
depin.faqCanOperatorSeeQ: Can a node operator see the content they host?
depin.faqCanOperatorSeeA: Protected content is stored as encrypted segments and the host does not receive playback keys. Public content remains publicly viewable through DeHub by design.
depin.faqHowMuchQ: How much will a node operator receive?
depin.faqHowMuchA: There is no fixed rate or forecast. Verified contribution may receive a share of a revenue-funded reward pool after an epoch closes. Rewards are not guaranteed, and electricity, bandwidth and hardware costs may exceed any reward.
depin.faqSoftwareAvailableQ: Is the node software available now?
depin.faqSoftwareAvailableA: A lightweight, browser-based tier is available today: sign in and opt in on this page, and your open tab becomes a node while it stays open. A heavier, always-on desktop node is a stated future direction — it does not exist yet.
depin.faqInstallNeededQ: Do I need to install anything for the browser node?
depin.faqInstallNeededA: No. It runs entirely in the tab using your browser's local storage. Closing the tab stops your node; there is no background service and no install.
depin.ctaTitle: Launch only when failure is safe.
depin.ctaBody: Origin fallback, encrypted protected media and verified work come before public node rewards.
depin.footerNote: DePin participation is a contribution service, not an investment product. Availability, eligibility and rewards may change.

commonGround.reminderBody: Most disagreements are not a choice between two extremes. When a question feels like either-or, there is usually a third option somewhere in the middle.
